mainEntity.name: Is Floatboat a drop-in replacement for Claude Cowork?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Cowork is a user-initiated desktop agent in Anthropic's ecosystem. Floatboat is a Calendar-Driven proactive agent OS where events and deadlines trigger pipelines. For drop-in open-source Cowork clones, evaluate Eigent, OpenWork, or Open Cowork.

mainEntity.name: Which open-source alternative is most like Claude Cowork?

acceptedAnswer.text: Open Cowork and Eigent market Cowork-like desktop experiences; OpenWork emphasizes portable skills across agents. PawWork optimizes for non-technical users and provider breadth. Compare sandbox models and OS support against your constraints.

mainEntity.name: When is Claude Cowork still the best choice?

acceptedAnswer.text: When you want Anthropic-managed execution, connector depth, remote sessions across devices, and you primarily initiate knowledge-work tasks yourself or on explicit schedules — especially if open-source maintenance overhead is undesirable.

mainEntity.name: Do I need to stop using Cowork if I add another tool?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not necessarily. Many operators keep a desktop cowork tool for episodic file work and add calendar-driven execution for recurring calls and deadlines. Overlap is in delegated work, not trigger design.

mainEntity.name: Which alternative is best for meeting preparation?

acceptedAnswer.text: For recurring prep before calls, calendar-driven architectures fit best. Cowork helps when you manually start or schedule prep with connected apps. Compare pipeline articles for meeting prep and follow-up for details.
